name: Albert Park Circuit

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap circuit relation 280443 (© OSM contributors), start at its "start" node 9123374386; Turn 6 road-junction vertex replaced by a 50 m-radius arc fitted to the junction pavement seen on Vicmap Basemap aerial imagery (base.maps.vic.gov.au AERIAL_WM_256); alignment checked against the same imagery
sources.width: Published: ~12-15 m street circuit; 2022 rework widened Turns 1, 3, 6 (+7.5 m), 11 and 13 (formerly 13, 15) (AGPC / F1 2022 track-change releases). The aerial imagery shows the public-road configuration (lane markings, parked cars), so it was not used for widths
sources.elevation: Copernicus GLO-30 DSM (https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com/, tile S38 E144), robust median ~250 m. GA/ELVIS LiDAR was not practically queryable (order-based / service blocked)
sources.trim: Medium downforce: fast lakeside sweeps and long DRS runs after the 2022 changes, slightly lower drag than Spa
sources.pitLimit: FIA Australian GP event notes: pit lane speed limit 80 km/h
sources.pitLoss: Typical F1 pit-stop loss ~19-20 s at Melbourne after the 2022 pit-lane widening (F1/Pirelli strategy previews); approximate
sources.raceLaps: FIA 2026 Australian GP: 58 laps; not a sprint weekend

notes: 14-turn 2022+ numbering (old 9/10 chicane removed: old 11-16 are now 9-14). Turn 7/8 apex placement on the lakeside sweeps is approximate. Elevation range is only a few metres; a 30 m surface model resolves only the broad trend.
